title: Artificial intelligence in education: The three paradigms
explain_beginner: This paper looks at how artificial intelligence has been used in education over time. The authors describe three stages. In the first, AI teaches and learners just receive. In the second, learners work together with AI. In the third, learners take charge and AI supports them. The paper argues that education is moving toward the third stage, where learners have more control and learning becomes more personal. This matters because it shows how AI tools may change teaching, shifting power from the system to the learner.
explain_business: This paper argues that AI in education is moving through three stages, ending with learners in control and AI adapting to them. For leaders, the practical message is that products and strategies built around AI simply delivering content to passive students may become outdated. Instead, tools should support learner choice, personalization, and feedback loops where learner data informs the system. This informs decisions about where to invest in educational technology, how to design products, and how to prepare for a market that increasingly values learner agency and data-driven personalization.
explain_practitioner: This position paper categorizes AI in education into three paradigms. Paradigm One uses AI to model knowledge and direct cognitive learning, with learners as recipients. Paradigm Two uses AI to support learning, with learners as collaborators. Paradigm Three uses AI to empower learning, with learners exercising agency. The authors argue the field is shifting toward the third paradigm, which emphasizes learner agency, personalization, reflection, and iterative, data-driven, learner-centered design. The key result is a framework describing this trend, not an experiment. It offers a lens for positioning AIEd systems and research.
